files.patch:
@@ -1,1 +1,7 @@
 def change
+def destroy
+  key = current_account.api_keys.active.find(params[:id])
+  key.update!(revoked_at: Time.current)
+  Audit::Recorder.call(account: current_account, action: "api_key.revoked", key_id: key.id)
+  head :no_content
+end
 end

topics.title: Revoking a key
paragraphs: destroy looks the key up through current_account.api_keys.active, so another account's key or an already revoked one is a 404 rather than a silent success. It sets revoked_at and returns 204. No authorization call is shown here; whether api_keys.manage is enforced depends on a before_action in the PR below.

topics.title: Where the stack comes together
paragraphs: Audit::Recorder comes from #411 and ApiKey with its active scope from #412. The request spec asserts both the revoked state and the recorded action, which is the first test that exercises the two lower PRs together.
